'''Florencia Canelli''' is since 2021 the appointed Swiss scientific delegate<ref>{{Cite web |last=SERI |first=State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation |title=CERN, the European Organisation for Nuclear Research, Geneva |url=https://www.sbfi.admin.ch/sbfi/en/home/research-and-innovation/international-cooperation-r-and-i/international-research-organisations/cern.html |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=www.sbfi.admin.ch |language=en}}</ref> to the [https://council.web.cern.ch/en CERN council], the supreme decision-making authority of the CERN Organization.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tschui |first=Silvia |date=12 June 2022 |title="Wissenschaft ist keine Glaubenssache" |url=https://www.blick.ch/life/wissen/naturwissenschaften/cern-physikerin-florencia-canelli-ueber-lehren-aus-der-pandemie-wissenschaft-ist-keine-glaubenssache-id17566802.html |access-date=16 September 2024 |work=Blick |pages=1–5}}</ref>  From 2021-2024, she was appointed chair of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]] division of particles and field (C11).<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=C11 |first=C11 |date=2021-03-05 |title=C11: Members 2021-2024 - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/commissions/c11-particles-and-fields/c11-members/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>  From 2021-2023, she was co-coordinator of the physics program of the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] collaboration,<ref>https://cms-docdb.cern.ch/cgi-bin/PublicDocDB/RetrieveFile?docid=3798</ref> a CERN experiment with over 3000 physicists.  In 2010, Canelli was awarded the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]] Young scientist prize, an international prize awarded to one experimental and one theoretical physicist per year, for "her pioneering contribution to the identification and precision measurements of rare phenomenon through the use of advanced analysis techniques to separate very small signals from large background processes at the Tevatron collider."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-07-11 |title=IUPAP Awards Young Scientist Prize in Particle Physics |url=https://www.interactions.org/press-release/iupap-awards-young-scientist-prize-particle-physics |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=Interactions |language=en}}</ref>   She has been an author on four multi-purpose collider experiments, namely the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS experiment]] and [[ATLAS experiment]] at the [[CERN]] [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]], and the [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF experiment]] and [[DØ experiment|D0 experiment]] at the [[Fermilab]] [[Tevatron]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6361-2117 |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=orcid.org}}</ref>  She is currently a full professor at the [[University of Zurich]], [https://www.physik.uzh.ch/en Physics Institute], specializing in [[particle physics]].   

== Early life and education ==
Florencia Canelli was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1973. At a young age, her family moved to Asuncion, Paraguay, where she received much of her education.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-17 |title=UZH Magazin 1/22 by University of Zurich - Issuu |url=https://issuu.com/uzhch/docs/uzh_magazin_1_22 |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=issuu.com |pages=48–51 |language=en}}</ref>  After receiving the equivalent of a physics bachelor degree at the [[Universidad Nacional de Asunción]] (Paraguay), she continued her education at the Instituto Balseiro in Bariloche, Argentina, before beginning her PhD studies in particle physics at the [[University of Rochester]] in the U.S. under the supervision of Tom Ferbel.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valich |first=Lindsey |date=2022-03-24 |title=Thomas Ferbel remembered as inspiring mentor and distinguished particle physicist |url=https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/thomas-ferbel-remembered-distinguished-particle-physicist-516552/ |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=News Center |language=en-US}}</ref>  Her PhD thesis, studying the properties of the top quark with data from the [[DØ experiment|D0 experiment]], introduced the so-called "matrix element" technique to improve measurements from collider detectors, and won several awards for this work, including the [https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/mitsuyoshi-tanaka-dissertation Mitsuyoshi Tanaka Dissertation Award], from APS.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-07-11 |title=IUPAP Awards Young Scientist Prize in Particle Physics |url=https://www.interactions.org/press-release/iupap-awards-young-scientist-prize-particle-physics |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=Interactions |language=en}}</ref>  
== Career ==
After her PhD, she became a postdoc at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] on the [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF]] experiment at [[Fermilab]] from 2003-2006.  During this time, she led efforts to estimate the energy scale of quarks produced in collisions,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bhatti |first1=A. |last2=Canelli |first2=F. |last3=Heinemann |first3=B. |last4=Adelman |first4=J. |last5=Ambrose |first5=D. |last6=Arguin |first6=J. -F. |last7=Barbaro-Galtieri |first7=A. |last8=Budd |first8=H. |last9=Chung |first9=Y. S. |last10=Chung |first10=K. |last11=Cooper |first11=B. |last12=Currat |first12=C. |last13=D'Onofrio |first13=M. |last14=Dorigo |first14=T. |last15=Erbacher |first15=R. |date=2006-10-15 |title=Determination of the jet energy scale at the Collider Detector at Fermilab |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168900206011053 |journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment |volume=566 |issue=2 |pages=375–412 |doi=10.1016/j.nima.2006.05.269 |issn=0168-9002|arxiv=hep-ex/0510047 |bibcode=2006NIMPA.566..375B }}</ref> significantly contributing to the experiment's results and improving the precision of numerous measurements.  

In 2006, she accepted a prestigious [https://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/robert_wilson/ Wilson Fellow] at Fermilab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fermilab {{!}} For Physicists & Engineers {{!}} Fellowships |url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/robert_wilson/past.html |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=www.fnal.gov}}</ref>  During her tenure as convener of the CDF top-quark group, the group made the first observation of the single production of top quarks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=CDF Collaboration |last2=Aaltonen |first2=T. |last3=Adelman |first3=J. |last4=Akimoto |first4=T. |last5=Álvarez González |first5=B. |last6=Amerio |first6=S. |last7=Amidei |first7=D. |last8=Anastassov |first8=A. |last9=Annovi |first9=A. |last10=Antos |first10=J. |last11=Apollinari |first11=G. |last12=Apresyan |first12=A. |last13=Arisawa |first13=T. |last14=Artikov |first14=A. |last15=Ashmanskas |first15=W. |date=2009-08-24 |title=Observation of Electroweak Single Top-Quark Production |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.092002 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=103 |issue=9 |article-number=092002 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.092002|pmid=19792788 |arxiv=0903.0885 |bibcode=2009PhRvL.103i2002A |hdl=10902/2061 }}</ref> 

In 2008, she became an assistant professor at the [[University of Chicago]], and began her involvement on the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] experiment at [[CERN]], while continuing on the CDF experiment. She was awarded the Sloan Research Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=sloan.org |language=en}}</ref> in 2009.   In 2009, she was promoted to Scientist 1 at Fermilab, and in 2011, was promoted to associate professor at University of Chicago.  

Canelli was part of the team at CDF that found evidence for the [[Higgs boson]] in 2012, as well as the ATLAS team that co-discovered the Higgs boson at the LHC on July 4th, 2012.  

In 2012, Canelli moved to Switzerland, becoming associate professor at the [[University of Zurich]], and later joining the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] experiment.  Her group has helped construct the CMS barrel pixel detector, installed in 2017, and studied a wide range of physics processes related to the Higgs boson, top quark, and beyond the Standard Model.   She has co-led the CMS top quark group, and from 2021-2023 was the co-coordinator of the entire CMS physics program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Highlights from CMS - Dr. Florencia Canelli - Conference on High Energy Physics (EPS-HEP) 2023 - Events - DESY video - livestreaming and video recordings |url=https://video.desy.de/channel/video/Highlights-from-CMS-2D-Dr2E-Florencia-Canelli/3cb77a07e3324acfbb3c321b31109d65/162 |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=video.desy.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Castelvecchi |first1=Davide |last2=Gibney |first2=Elizabeth |date=2022-04-07 |title=Particle's surprise mass threatens to upend the standard model |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-022-01014-5 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=604 |issue=7905 |pages=225–226 |doi=10.1038/d41586-022-01014-5|pmid=35393589 |bibcode=2022Natur.604..225C |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gibney |first=Elizabeth |date=2022-05-25 |title=How the revamped Large Hadron Collider will hunt for new physics |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-022-01388-6 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=605 |issue=7911 |pages=604–607 |doi=10.1038/d41586-022-01388-6|pmid=35614240 |bibcode=2022Natur.605..604G |url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

Canelli has been appointed to several high-level positions in international bodies, serving as chair of the Particles and fields commission (C11)<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=C11 |first=C11 |date=2021-03-19 |title=C11: Particles and Fields - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/commissions/c11-particles-and-fields/ |access-date=2024-09-13 |language=en-US}}</ref> of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] from 2021-2024, and as Swiss scientific delegate to the [https://council.web.cern.ch/en CERN council] since 2021. 

In 2025, Canelli was elected as a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for distinguished leadership in physics at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN and for significant contributions to the study of the top quark at the Large Hadron Collider and at the Tevatron at Fermilab".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?q=canelli&af=false|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref>

== Published works ==
Canelli has over 1700 [https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=25&page=1&q=find%20a%20Florencia%20canelli%20and%20type%20p publications], mainly on the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]], [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]], [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF]] and [[DØ experiment|D0]] experiments. 

== Personal life ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=September 2024}}
Canelli is married to experimental particle physicist, Prof. Ben Kilminster. They have two children.

==Leadership in international organizations==
* since 2022:   Swiss scientific delegate to [[CERN Council]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-27 |title=Council - Composition as from January 2022 {{!}} CERN Council |url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/council-composition-january-2022 |access-date=2025-01-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927072337/https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/council-composition-january-2022 |archive-date=27 September 2022 }}</ref> Vice-President of the Council as of 2025<ref>{{Cite web |title=Council - Composition as from January 2025 {{!}} CERN Council |url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/council-composition-january-2025 |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=council.web.cern.ch}}</ref>
* 2021-2024:   Chair of the commission Particles and Fields (C11) of [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=C11 |first=C11 |date=2021-03-05 |title=C11: Members 2021-2024 - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/c11-members-2021-2024/ |access-date=2025-01-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2017-2020:   Member of Fermilab Physics Advisory Committee (PAC)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-12-24 |title=Members {{!}} Physics Advisory Committee |url=http://pac.fnal.gov/members/ |access-date=2025-01-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171224072245/http://pac.fnal.gov/members/ |archive-date=24 December 2017 }}</ref>
* 2017-2021:   Secretary of the commission Particles and Fields (C11) of [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=iupap |date=2021-12-01 |title=C11: Members 2017-2021 - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/c11-members-2017-2021-2/ |access-date=2025-01-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2014-2017:   Regular member of the commission Particles and Fields (C11) of [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=C11: Members (2014-2017) {{!}} IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://archive2.iupap.org/c11-members-2014-2017/ |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=archive2.iupap.org}}</ref>
* 2013-2021:   Swiss representative to the [[CMS experiment|CMS]] management board<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-12 |title=Organisation {{!}} CMS Experiment |url=http://cms.cern/collaboration/organisation |access-date=2025-01-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512154929/http://cms.cern/collaboration/organisation |archive-date=12 May 2017 }}</ref>
* 2016-2019:   Swiss representative to the [[Cherenkov Telescope Array]] Council

==Leadership in experimental collaborations==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=September 2024}}
* 2021-2023:   Physics co-coordinator for the CMS experiment
* 2018-2020:   Convener of the CMS top-quark group
* 2015-2016:   Convener of the CMS "Very Heavy Fermions" (VFS) group
* 2007-2009:   Convener of the CDF top-quark group
* 2005-2007:   Convener of the CDF top-quark mass group
* 2003-2004:   Convener of the CDF jet-energy and resolution group
